expected.name: Rebecca Kanner
expected.description:
Rebecca Kanner crossed the line at Fort Benning, Georgia during the November 2000 SOA Watch vigil. Sentenced to 6 months, $500 fine.

Each year on the November anniversary of the assassination of six Jesuits, their housekeeper, and her daughter at the University of Central America in San Salvador in 1989, peace activists gather at the gates of Fort Benning, Georgia, site of the U.S. Army School of the Americas / Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC), to commemorate the dead and to call for the school's closure. Hundreds have crossed the line onto the base over four decades of vigils; many have served federal sentences ranging from 30 days to a year for trespass.

operations.name: A. H. McMillan

expected.charges: Federal prosecution under the Espionage Act of 1917 and/or the Sedition Act of 1918.

updates.sentence: 20 years — four concurrent 20-year terms; conviction subsequently reversed

operations.source: Institutional history with participant recollections and quoted judicial correspondence: https://wol.jw.org/en/wol/pc/r1/lp-e/1989320/0/0 . Names A. Hugh Macmillan among defendants; June 21, 1918 sentencing, concurrent terms. March 25 departure from Atlanta penitentiary is distinct from March 26 federal release on bail in Brooklyn, used here as custody endpoint. Convictions reversed May 14, 1919; prosecution withdrawn May 5, 1920. Preserve existing June 21 custody start; do not equate May arrest warrant with continuous imprisonment.
